title: Which Transactions Count as Spending Within a Closing Benefit Period
content:
What was spent from a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card in the benefit period being closed is counted from a different set of that period's transactions according to what else that period contains.

**The rule.** What was spent from the card in that period is counted from the transactions that settled alone, where the period carries a transaction the card network refused; from the transactions that settled together with those still only authorised, where the period carries no refused transaction but carries one still only authorised; and from every transaction posted in the period in every other case.

**Points of judgement.**

1. A refused transaction is the deciding fact of the first row. It is enough that one transaction in the period was refused by the card network; the amount refused is itself never counted as spending.
2. The second row is reached only where no refused transaction stands in the period. A transaction still only authorised is added to what settled.
3. The third row is reached where the period carries neither a refused transaction nor one still only authorised, and every transaction posted in the period is counted.

**Worked through on hypothetical entries.** A closing period shows purchases of 30.00 USD settled, 22.50 USD settled, 18.00 USD authorised and not yet settled and 12.00 USD refused. A refused transaction stands, so what was spent is counted from the settled transactions alone: 52.50 USD. Strike the refused entry and the same period gives 52.50 USD together with the 18.00 USD still only authorised, that is 70.50 USD. Strike the authorised entry as well and every transaction posted is counted, giving 52.50 USD.
